text:
noah: hey folks, first day trying to spin up the dev db. using postgres:15-alpine in compose and init keeps failing with:

`initdb: could not change permissions of directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data": Operation not permitted`

I tried `chown` on the host dir but still same. compose mounts `./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` and I ran `sudo chown 999:999 pgdata` (999 is postgres uid). any ideas?

rachel: welcome! two axes to check: 1) alpine image runs as a different uid sometimes and mac/linux host bind mounts can change perms. 2) postgres alpine images historically run init as root then switch, but bind mounts on non-Linux fs (or with certain Docker settings) can block chown.

noah: i'm on Ubuntu WSL (WSL2) but my repo is on a Windows-mounted drive (D:\code). i suspect the mount is the issue.

ops-bot: ops-bot posted: "volume mount on non-Linux fs detected for container postgres (host path: D:\code\project\pgdata)"

matt: yep, if the project dir lives on a Windows filesystem the container cannot change ownership. options: a) move the repo into the WSL filesystem (~/project) or b) use a named volume instead of a host bind: `pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`. Named volumes live in Docker/WSL and support chown.

noah: moved the repo into WSL home and removed the explicit host mount; switched compose to a named volume and restarted. new error now: `initdb: locale "en_US.utf8" not recognized`

elyse: that's because alpine images don't include glibc locales by default. You can either: 1) use the non-alpine postgres image (e.g., `postgres:15` or `postgres:15-bullseye`) which has locales, or 2) set initdb to use the C locale by adding env `POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: "--encoding=UTF8 --locale=C"`, or 3) install `glibc-i18n` in the image (more involved). For quick local dev we normally switch to `postgres:15` image in the onboarding compose.

noah: switched to `postgres:15` and the DB came up cleanly. migrations ran. thanks! i'll open a tiny PR to update the onboarding notes: mention (1) avoid binding pgdata to Windows mounts, (2) prefer named volumes or WSL filesystem, (3) caution about alpine locales and recommend non-alpine images for dev.

matt: perfect — tag me on the PR, and welcome aboard :tada:
